title: Acceptance corridor and dependency contract for prompt-eval PRD
creator: Evelyn Thompson
description: Scope: Define clear acceptance corridors (pass/fail criteria, guardrails, and rollback lanes) and a signed dependency contract between Product, Engineering, Design, and Legal for the Prompt Evaluation PRD. This ticket coordinates signoffs, captures unresolved questions, and locks acceptance criteria for the PRD slice that enables automated evals tied to model rollouts and telemetry. The objective is to avoid last-minute scope creep during rollout and to make signoff deterministic for both Hosted and Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Product, Engineering, Design, and Legal have signed a one-page dependency contract that enumerates responsibilities and SLAs for the prompt-eval feature
A canonical acceptance checklist exists (document link in linked_artifacts) covering functional tests, privacy/data residency, perf SLOs, and UI behaviour for both hosted and dedicated modes
Design has delivered final annotated mocks (desktop/mobile) and a component inventory with accessibility notes
Engineering has validated performance budget: median end-to-end eval latency < 1200ms at target QPS with batching profile and provided a mitigation plan for 2x load
Legal has confirmed allowable telemetry fields and redaction requirements; security review completed and documented
Rollout plan includes canary cohort definition, automated regression detectors, and explicit rollback triggers in Console
All cross-team dependencies listed below are assigned owners and have either a pull request or clear deliverable ETA
decisions: Use server-side prefix caching as the primary cost control for eval runs; Eng to own implementation with a feature flag
Telemetry schema v1 will exclude raw prompt texts; instead store prompt hashes + metadata for eval matching; Legal approved approach
Design agreed to a condensed results panel for the Console to reduce cognitive load during canary review
linked_artifacts: GitHub: eng/telemetry-schema#142 - draft schema and migration plan
